episode_title: Shadow AI and tokenmaxxing: what your AI habits could cost you with Amy Gebhardt

real_qa.q: What is token maxing and why has it become a concern for businesses adopting AI tools?
real_qa.r: Token maxing is a proxy for productivity or proof that employees are engaging with AI, where companies allow unlimited token consumption with no budgets or limitations to demonstrate technology adoption. The issue is that token consumption does not tell the full story of actual productivity or value, and tokens make the financial impact harder to connect and easier to overspend without thinking about real costs.

real_qa.q: How does AI consumption-based pricing differ from traditional cloud consumption models in terms of predictability?
real_qa.r: AI consumption-based pricing is particularly hard to forecast compared to cloud consumption models, which were fairly predictable. With AI, consumption is heavily dependent on human behavior and scattered throughout different roles in the organization since everyone has access to AI and can engage with it.
real_qa.requete: AI consumption-based pricing vs cloud models

real_qa.q: How did Unit 42 demonstrate the speed increase of AI-assisted cyber attacks compared to manual hacking?
real_qa.r: Unit 42 investigated an intrusion where a human attacker used multiple frontier AI agents to work through more than 50 MITRE attack techniques in under 10 hours, whereas the equivalent activity could normally take a human operator around two weeks. This compressed two weeks of intrusion activity into under 10 hours.
real_qa.requete: Unit 42 AI agents cyber attack 10 hours

real_qa.q: What are the key security questions organizations should ask when adopting AI tools internally?
real_qa.r: Organizations should ask: Do you know what credentials are being used for AI tools and workflows and where they are stored? How can you shut down access quickly if needed? What access are you actually giving to AI tools—for example, full file access when only specific files are needed? Understanding boundaries and permissions is critical because giving permission to read files means the AI will read all files, not just the ones intended.
real_qa.requete: AI tool security questions enterprise adoption

real_qa.q: How can defenders use AI to detect and respond to machine-speed attacks more quickly?
real_qa.r: Defenders need to have AI or automation already in place to get eyes on glass quicker, as the basic defense tactics remain the same but are executed at higher speed. The challenge is that blue teams are behind right now because they have to play by the rules, get approvals, and set things up correctly, while attackers can point frontier models at targets with no pre-context and execute immediately.

real_qa.q: What is the 'living off AI' attack technique and why is it a concern?
real_qa.r: Living off AI refers to attackers using a victim's own internal AI infrastructure and resources to run part of their attack operation after stealing cloud keys. This means businesses need to think not only about how employees use AI but also how attackers could abuse the AI tools and infrastructure the business already has, treating AI as core infrastructure requiring inventory, access controls, rate limits, logging, and clear ownership.
